questions.q: Which method is used when the regressor is correlated with the error term?
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] IV methods give consistent estimates under endogeneity.

questions.q: The paradox of thrift implies that an increase in the saving propensity may:
options: Reduce income without raising total saving
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] Higher saving lowers demand and income; total saving may not rise (it can even fall if investment is induced).

questions.q: In a liquidity trap:
options: LM is horizontal; monetary policy is ineffective
LM is vertical; fiscal policy is ineffective
IS is vertical; monetary policy is effective
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] At very low interest rates money demand is infinitely elastic, so extra money is just held; only fiscal policy works.

questions.q: A leptokurtic distribution has β₂:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] Leptokurtic (peaked) curves have kurtosis above 3.

questions.q: Fisher effect states that:
options: Nominal rate = real rate + expected inflation
Money is neutral in short run
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] i = r + πᵉ.

questions.q: The 'voting with the feet' model is by:
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Charles Tiebout (1956): local public goods and mobility.

questions.q: The permanent income hypothesis predicts that a one-time lottery win will be:
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] Transitory income has a very low MPC; it is mostly saved and spread over time.

questions.q: With 4 seasons and an intercept, how many seasonal dummies should be used?
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] m − 1 = 3; using 4 causes the dummy variable trap (perfect multicollinearity).

questions.q: In the Harrod–Domar model, if s = 24% and v = 4, growth rate is:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] g = s/v = 24/4 = 6%.

questions.q: Union Budget 2026-27 fiscal deficit target is:
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Down from 4.4% (RE) in 2025-26.

questions.q: The 'impossible trinity' says a country cannot simultaneously have:
options: Floating rate, inflation targeting and fiscal policy
Low inflation, high growth and full employment
Fixed exchange rate, free capital flows and independent monetary policy
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Only two of the three can be chosen at a time.

questions.q: Income terms of trade is defined as:
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Dorrance's income TOT measures the capacity to import.

questions.q: Trade diversion in a customs union means:
options: Imports shift from a lower-cost outsider to a higher-cost member
Imports shift from a higher-cost member to a lower-cost outsider
Domestic production replaced by member imports
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Viner (1950): trade diversion reduces welfare.

questions.q: Kitchin cycles last about:
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] Kitchin: short inventory cycles of about 40 months.

questions.q: The golden rule of capital accumulation requires:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Phelps: steady-state consumption per worker is maximised.

questions.q: The first bank nationalisation (14 banks) happened in:
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] July 1969; six more in 1980.

questions.q: The Cambridge cash balance equation is:
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] k is the fraction of income held as money (k = 1/V).

questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission was chaired by:
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Arvind Panagariya; award period 2026–31; states' share kept at 41%.

questions.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Baumol gave sales-revenue maximisation. Monopolistic competition is Chamberlin's; revealed preference is Samuelson's; the contract curve is Edgeworth's.

questions.q: According to the Tendulkar method, poverty in India in 2011-12 was:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Rangarajan gave 29.5% for the same year.

questions.q: India's TFR according to NFHS-5 is:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] Below replacement level.

questions.q: The theory of comparative advantage was given by:
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Ricardo (1817), Principles of Political Economy and Taxation.

questions.q: The 'Market for Lemons' (1970) deals with:
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Akerlof showed hidden quality information before trade (adverse selection) can make markets collapse.

questions.q: In the Cournot duopoly with zero costs and linear demand, total industry output is what fraction of the competitive output?
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Each firm produces 1/3 of the competitive output, so together 2/3.

questions.q: FEMA replaced FERA in:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.

questions.q: PM-KISAN gives eligible farmers per year:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] In three equal instalments of ₹2,000.

questions.q: Malthus' theory says population grows in:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] Food supply grows in arithmetic progression.

questions.q: Elasticity of substitution of a Cobb–Douglas production function is:
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Cobb–Douglas always has σ = 1, whatever the returns to scale.

questions.q: 'Tragedy of the commons' was written by:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] Garrett Hardin, Science (1968).

questions.q: The WTO came into existence on:
questions.explanation: [International Economics] The Marrakesh Agreement was signed on 15 April 1994; WTO started on 1 January 1995.

questions.q: NITI Aayog was set up on:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] It replaced the Planning Commission by a cabinet resolution.

questions.q: If TR = 100Q − 2Q² and TC = 20Q + Q², profit-maximising output is:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] π = 80Q − 3Q²; dπ/dQ = 80 − 6Q = 0 gives Q = 13.33.

questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] Adopted 1997; in force 2005.

questions.q: Arrow's impossibility theorem does NOT include which condition?
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Arrow's conditions: unrestricted domain, Pareto, IIA, non-dictatorship (and transitivity). Lump-sum transfers are from the second welfare theorem.

questions.q: Consumer equilibrium in indifference curve analysis requires:
options: MRSxy = Px/Py with the IC convex to the origin
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Tangency (MRS = price ratio) is the first-order condition; convexity of the IC is the second-order condition.

questions.q: Coase theorem requires:
options: Clearly defined property rights and low transaction costs
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Then private bargaining reaches an efficient outcome.

questions.q: National income (NNP at factor cost) equals:
options: NNP at market prices − net indirect taxes
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] NNP at FC = NNP at MP − (indirect taxes − subsidies).

questions.q: Variance of a binomial distribution with n = 100 and p = 0.2 is:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] npq = 100 × 0.2 × 0.8 = 16.

questions.q: Ricardian equivalence is associated with:
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] Robert Barro (1974): debt-financed tax cuts do not raise consumption because people save for future taxes.

questions.q: Basel III introduced:
options: Three pillars for the first time
Capital conservation buffer, leverage ratio and liquidity ratios (LCR, NSFR)
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] Three pillars came with Basel II; Basel III added buffers and liquidity rules.

questions.q: For two positive numbers, AM = 10 and HM = 6.4. GM is:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] GM² = AM × HM = 64, so GM = 8.

questions.q: In a zero-sum game, a saddle point exists when:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] The value of the game equals both, and pure strategies are optimal.

questions.q: Under perfect capital mobility and a fixed exchange rate (Mundell–Fleming), which policy is effective?
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] Monetary expansion causes outflows that force the central bank to reverse it; fiscal expansion attracts inflows and is accommodated.

questions.q: The Leontief paradox (1953) found that the USA exported:
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Contrary to H–O, US exports were relatively labour-intensive.

questions.q: Sex ratio in NFHS-5 was:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] Females per 1000 males; Census 2011 gave 943.

questions.q: The determinant of [4 2; 3 5] is:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] 4 × 5 − 2 × 3 = 14.

questions.q: Two-gap model was given by:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Saving gap and foreign exchange gap (1966).

questions.q: Demand functions are homogeneous of degree:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] Doubling all prices and income leaves demand unchanged (no money illusion).

questions.q: Which is NOT a reason for a downward-sloping AD curve?
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] The ratchet effect belongs to Duesenberry's consumption theory, not to AD.

questions.q: The Union Budget is presented under Article:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Annual Financial Statement.

questions.q: If MPC = 0.8, the investment multiplier is:
questions.explanation: [Macro Economics] k = 1/(1 − MPC) = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.q: The simplex method was developed by:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] George Dantzig, 1947.

questions.q: Wagner's law states that:
options: Public expenditure falls as economy grows
Debt should be repaid in booms
Public expenditure grows faster than national income
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Adolph Wagner's law of increasing state activity.

questions.q: Which is a club good?
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Excludable but non-rival (up to capacity).

questions.q: The absorption approach to BoP was given by:
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Alexander (1952): trade balance = output − absorption.

questions.q: Q = AL^0.6 K^0.5 shows:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] α + β = 1.1 > 1, so increasing returns to scale.

questions.q: If price elasticity of demand is 2 and price is ₹40, marginal revenue is:
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] MR = P(1 − 1/e) = 40(1 − 1/2) = ₹20.

questions.q: The New Industrial Policy was announced on:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Along with the Union Budget 1991-92.

questions.q: Replacement level total fertility rate is:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] About 2.1 children per woman.

questions.q: Hawkins–Simon conditions relate to:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] All principal minors of (I − A) must be positive for a viable solution.

questions.q: Under the Gauss–Markov assumptions, OLS estimators are:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] Best Linear Unbiased Estimators. Normality is not needed for this result.

questions.q: If byx = 0.8 and bxy = 0.2, the correlation coefficient is:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] r = √(0.8 × 0.2) = √0.16 = 0.4 (positive because both coefficients are positive).

questions.q: The GST Council is provided for under Article:
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment (2016).

questions.q: Hotelling rule says that the rent of an exhaustible resource rises at:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] Harold Hotelling (1931).

questions.q: The VB-G RAM G Act, which replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026, guarantees how many days of rural work?
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Raised from 100 to 125 days per household per year.

questions.q: Critical minimum effort thesis was given by:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Harvey Leibenstein (1957).

questions.q: Endogenous growth theory based on R&D and ideas is linked with:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Paul Romer (1990); Nobel 2018.

questions.q: Which committee recommended the flexible inflation targeting framework (2014)?
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] Urjit Patel Committee report, January 2014.

questions.q: Coase theorem (1960) suggests externalities can be solved through:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] With low transaction costs, bargaining is efficient.

questions.q: For Q = 20P⁻², price elasticity of demand is:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] For Q = aP⁻ᵇ elasticity is constant at −b.

questions.q: Brundtland Report is titled:
questions.explanation: [Environment & Demography] 1987, World Commission on Environment and Development.

questions.q: Primary deficit is:
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] It shows borrowing for current needs excluding past interest.

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee has how many members?
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] Three from RBI (incl. Governor) and three external members.

questions.q: The HDI uses which mean to combine its three indices (since 2010)?
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Geometric mean, so a low value in one dimension cannot be fully offset.

questions.q: An advance is classified as NPA when dues are overdue for more than:
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] The 90-day norm.

questions.q: Spurious regression is suspected when:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] Granger–Newbold rule of thumb: R² greater than the DW statistic with non-stationary series.

questions.q: Lerner's index of monopoly power equals:
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] L = (P − MC)/P = 1/|ed| at profit maximum.

questions.q: The kinked demand curve model explains:
questions.explanation: [Micro Economics] Sweezy (1939): rivals match price cuts but not rises, giving a kink and a gap in MR, so price stays rigid.

questions.q: In the cobweb model Qd = a − bP(t), Qs = c + dP(t−1), the path converges if:
questions.explanation: [Mathematical Economics] Price oscillations shrink when supply responds less than demand to price.

questions.q: Which theory explains intra-industry trade?
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Economies of scale and love of variety give two-way trade in similar goods.

questions.q: A Durbin–Watson statistic close to 0 indicates:
questions.explanation: [Statistics & Econometrics] d ≈ 2(1 − ρ); ρ near +1 gives d near 0.

questions.q: The floor of RBI's LAF corridor since 2022 is the:
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] SDF = repo − 25 bps; it does not need collateral.

questions.q: Economic Survey 2025-26 projects FY27 real GDP growth at:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Tabled 29 January 2026.

questions.q: Broad money M3 equals:
questions.explanation: [Money & Banking] M3 = M1 + net time deposits of banks.

questions.q: Gini coefficient is calculated from the Lorenz curve as:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] A = area between equality line and Lorenz curve; A + B = total area under the line.

questions.q: MSP is announced on the recommendation of:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (1965).

questions.q: In the Solow model, a higher saving rate raises in the long run:
questions.explanation: [Growth & Development] Steady-state growth depends only on technical progress.

questions.q: Exchange rate overshooting model was given by:
questions.explanation: [International Economics] Rudiger Dornbusch (1976), with sticky goods prices.

questions.q: The four Labour Codes came into force on:
questions.explanation: [Indian Economy] Notified for implementation on 21 Nov 2025.

questions.q: 'Equal marginal sacrifice' principle leads to:
questions.explanation: [Public Economics] Least aggregate sacrifice: tax the richest first until incomes are equal at the top.
